officialInventory.summary: Uganda Wildlife Authority manages the wildlife conservation areas and states their counts (10 national parks, 12 wildlife reserves, 5 community wildlife management areas, 13 wildlife sanctuaries) but its website names only the national parks and 11 wildlife reserves. The legal declarations are statutory instruments under the Uganda Wildlife Act (most from 2003, SI 41–64 of 2003), indexed on ULII. The National Forestry Authority manages 506 central forest reserves (no list published on its website); local forest reserves are managed by district governments.

statedCounts.quote: Uganda Wildlife Authority, (UWA) manages 10 National Parks
mandated to sustainably manage the country's 506 Central Forest Reserves (CFRs)

areas.name: Kibale National Park

legalStatus.text: Uganda Wildlife (Declaration of Wildlife Conservation Area) (Kibale National Park) Instrument, 2003 (SI 46 of 2003)

areas.name: Kidepo Valley National Park
areas.notes: UWA: 'First gazetted as a national park in 1962'; area is the UWA headline figure (1,442 km²). 2003-era declaration instrument not found on ULII.

areas.name: Murchison Falls National Park
areas.notes: UWA: 'Originally gazetted as a game reserve in 1926, the park was officially designated as one of Uganda's first national parks in 1952'; area is the UWA headline figure (3,840 km²); the UWA Karuma page gives 3,877 km² for the park.

areas.name: Rwenzori Mountains National Park
areas.notes: UWA: 'The park was gazetted in 1991, declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1994, and later designated a Ramsar Wetland ... in 2008'.

areas.name: Semuliki National Park
areas.notes: UWA: 'established as a forest reserve in 1932 and upgraded to national park status in 1993'; area 220 km² (UWA headline).

areas.name: Toro-Semliki Wildlife Reserve

legalStatus.text: Uganda Wildlife (Declaration of Wildlife Conservation Area) (Toro-Semliki Wildlife Reserve) Instrument, 2003 (SI 53 of 2003)

areas.name: Katonga Wildlife Reserve
areas.notes: UWA: 'with an area of 207 square kilometers was gazetted in 1964 as a game reserve ... became a Wildlife Reserve in 1996'. 2003-era declaration instrument not found on ULII.

areas.name: Ajai Wildlife Reserve

legalStatus.text: Uganda Wildlife (Declaration of Wildlife Conservation Area) (Ajais Wildlife Reserve) Instrument, 2003 (SI 52 of 2003)

areas.notes: UWA: 'Established in 1962 as the White Rhino Sanctuary. Established as Ajai Game Reserve in 1965'; 'Area 148km2 (15,800ha)' (the two figures are inconsistent on the UWA page). The 2003 SI title spells it 'Ajais'.

notEnumerated.reason: NFA states 506 CFRs (1,265,741 ha) but its CFR catalogue page does not list them; the declaring orders (Forest (Declaration of Central Forest Reserves) Orders) are on ULII but full text is blocked to automated fetch.
Managed by District Local Governments (NFA catalogue page); no list found.

notEnumerated.category: wildlife sanctuaries not found in legal records
notEnumerated.reason: UWA states 13 sanctuaries; only 5 declaration instruments (2003) were found on ULII and UWA's sanctuary page shows only Ziwa Rhino Sanctuary (privately run; legal status not verified).

notEnumerated.category: community wildlife areas not found in legal records
notEnumerated.reason: UWA states 5; only 4 declaration instruments (2003) were found on ULII.

gaps: ULII document pages are behind a Cloudflare challenge; only instrument titles, numbers and dates from the ULII search API were used. SI 60 of 2003 (gap in the series 41–64) could not be identified.

No 2003-era declaration instruments were found for Kidepo Valley, Murchison Falls, Rwenzori Mountains and Semuliki national parks or for Katonga, Karuma and Kigezi wildlife reserves; these may have been declared under earlier legislation (e.g. National Parks Act; National Parks (Declaration) (Amendment) Order, SI 76 of 1993).

UWA page areas are headline figures; the Kibale figure (321 km², identical to Bwindi) appears erroneous and was omitted; Ajai, Karuma and Kigezi pages give inconsistent km²/ha pairs (km² value recorded).
Whether East Madi is UWA's 12th wildlife reserve is inferred, not confirmed.
Ramsar sites and World Heritage sites (Bwindi, Rwenzori) are noted only where they coincide with a park.
No official coordinates were found for any area.

Wikidata QIDs were matched (search + entity check of label, P17 country and P31 type) only for national parks and selected major reserves; the Wikidata API was heavily rate-limited (HTTP 429) during this run, so other areas were not attempted or the lookup failed. A null QID does not mean no item exists.
